newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul central bank wants to keep supervisory power.
newsitem.headline: Seoul central bank wants to keep supervisory power.

text.p: South Korea's central Bank of Korea (BOK) should retain its supervisory functions to maintain a sound credit system, the BOK governor said on Thursday.
"I think it is not right to separate the role of bank supervision from the Bank of Korea," Lee Kyung-shick said in a prepared statement on the bank's 47th anniversary.
"Without that function, the central bank, as the final lender, will lose much of its ability to prevent and manage financial crises," Lee said.
Proposed reforms of rules governing the central bank should focus on guaranteeing neutrality and autonomy in establishing and implementing monetary policy, he said.

Earlier this month, a presidential commission for financial reforms proposed unifying the country's three financial watchdogs -- the Office of Bank Supervision, currently under the central bank, the Securities Supervisory Board and the Insurance Supervisory Board.
The commission said the unified financial watchdog should be under the direct control of the prime minister.
Officials at the finance ministry have said the bank supervisory function should be transferred to the ministry. That position has sparked a conflict between the ministry and the central bank.
